headline: Focused Prostate Treatment Matches Surgery Results, Cuts Complications
meta_description: NHS study of 3,500 men shows focal prostate cancer treatment works as well as surgery or radiotherapy while dramatically reducing side effects.
summary_short: A decade-long NHS study proves focal prostate treatment is as effective as traditional approaches—but with five times fewer sexual and bladder problems.
body:
Focal prostate cancer treatment works just as well as surgery or radiotherapy, according to a 10-year NHS study of nearly 3,500 men—but with a crucial advantage: it cuts the risk of erectile dysfunction and incontinence by five fold.

The findings represent a meaningful shift in how prostate cancer might be managed. Patients have long faced a difficult choice: aggressive treatments that work well but often damage sexual and urinary function, or watching and waiting. Focal therapy suggests a middle path, delivering cancer control without the same toll on quality of life.

For men diagnosed with prostate cancer, these results offer real hope. The ability to treat the disease effectively while preserving continence and sexual function could transform how thousands approach their diagnosis and recovery.
quick_facts: Focal treatment as effective as surgery or radiotherapy
Five-fold reduction in erectile dysfunction and incontinence risk
